decisions.rationale: In the title, 'myotonic dystrophy' is a disease name used as a modifier of the noun 'locus' (the myotonic dystrophy locus), so it is annotated as a Modifier rather than a standalone disease mention.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 3: Annotate disease mentions that are used as Modifiers for other concepts

decisions.rationale: 'myotonic dystrophy' here modifies 'kinase' in the gene/protein name 'myotonic dystrophy kinase (DMK)'. The disease name functions as a modifier of another concept, so it is annotated as a Modifier, not as a Specific Disease.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 3: Annotate disease mentions that are used as Modifiers for other concepts

decisions.rationale: 'myotonic dystrophy' in 'in which myotonic dystrophy (DM) has not been described' refers to the single specific disease DM, which has no further categorization. Minimum span is the full name.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 1: Specific Disease mentions; What to Annotate 5: minimum necessary span

decisions.rationale: 'DM' is the abbreviation defined as a synonym of 'myotonic dystrophy' in the parenthetical '(DM)'. Abbreviation definitions are separated into their own annotated mention, so the short form is annotated as a Specific Disease.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 6: Annotate all synonymous mentions (abbreviation definitions)

decisions.rationale: 'DM' in 'the rare ancestral DM mutation event' modifies the noun 'mutation' and so is a disease abbreviation used as a modifier of another concept, not a standalone disease reference.

decisions.rationale: 'DM' in 'the absence of DM in sub-Saharan Negroid peoples' refers to the disease itself as a standalone entity (the absence of the disease), so it is annotated as a Specific Disease.
